newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr subdued by protracted policy debate.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr subdued by protracted policy debate.

text.p: The Australian dollar loitered through another lacklustre session Tuesday with local trading bracketed by bids beneath US$0.7340 and offers atop US$0.7380.
Traders said the range trading mentality had been reinforced by another failed tilt at the downside offshore and saw no end to the dealock until the Reserve Bank made up its ming on rates.

The June balance of goods and services showed the largest surplus ever, but lit few lights being largely the product of bookkeeping for the sale of gold by the Reserve Bank. Imports were up 8.0 percent, perhaps heralding a long awaited pickup in domestic demand but not altering the immediate policy outlook.

By 5.00 pm (0700 GMT) the local currency was stuck in a rut at US$0.7370/75 having hardly moved from an early U$0.7364/69 and US$0.7360/65 late here Monday. It dipped as low as US$0.7335 offshore but the move was exagerrated by an illiquid market and the losses were soon recouped when modest bids appeared.
Dealers doubted the recent US$0.7310/7440 range would be troubled while the threat of another rate cut loomed.

Most expect the RBA to cut its cash rate by 0.5 point to 5.0 percent after its monthly board meeting on August 5. This would be the fifth easing since last July and, in a seminal event, take official rates below those in the U.S.

Traders reckoned such a move was largely priced into the dollar given it had fallen more than four cents since the last easing on May 23, but the market was wary in case the RBA chose to surprise once again.
A 0.75 point cut, for instance, would see the dollar testing US$0.7280 in a hurry and could fulfill technical predictions of a fresh downtrend to the 1995 low of US$0.7070.
In contrast, no move at all on August 6 would inspire speculation the easing cycle had actually ended and trigger a sharp short covering rally, perhaps back to US$0.7550.
Today's data provided little insight into what to expect.
The overall surplus on goods and services widened to A$1.96 billion from A$787 million in May, but A$1.8 billion reflected the RBA's sale of gold reserves which were included in exports.

Goods exports were thus up a whopping 23 percent and, on the surface, promised a big contribution to GDP growth from net exports. However, the Statistics Bureau said the gold would be taken from stocks so exactly offsetting their contribution in the exports measure.
Imports of both consumer and capital goods rose 14 percent in June, with the former largely boosted by car imports and the latter by the purchase of a A$200 million civil aircraft.

The lift in imports was still nothing like as emphatic enough to make the market question its central rate assumptions, a conclusion analysts also expected to make about building approvals and retail trade data out tomorrow and Thursday.

The dollar was mixed on the crosses where all sorts of currents were at work. The A$ was sharply higher on the pound, which suffered massive profit taking overnight, at 0.4511/16 stg from 0.4453/58 late Monday but lost ground on a rallying Kiwi to NZ$1.1395/12 from NZ$1.1422/42. It was firmer on the yen at 86.58/68 from 86.20/30 and unchanged in trade weighted terms at 57.6. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
